extracted.intended_audience: permit applicants, regulated entities, project developers, and regulators involved in UIC Class VI CO2 geologic sequestration permitting and EPA rulemaking stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory criteria for permitting Class VI Underground Injection Control (UIC) wells for CO2 geologic sequestration, including protection of underground sources of drinking water, area-of-review delineation, seismicity, construction/operation standards, and emergency/remedial requirements. Intended to inform permit application preparation and regulatory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Underground Sources of Drinking Water (USDWs)
rubrics_metrics.description: UIC regulations for Class VI wells authorize the injection of CO2 for geologic sequestration while protecting human health by ensuring the protection of underground sources of drinking water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major components to be included in UIC Class VI permits are detailed further in section VII.C.1.a.i(D)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Area of Review (AOR) delineation (40 CFR 146.84(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 40 CFR 146.84(a), the area of review is the region surrounding the geologic sequestration project where USDWs may be endangered by the injection activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The area of review is delineated using computational modeling that accounts for the physical and chemical properties of all phases of the injected carbon dioxide stream and is based on available site characterization, monitoring, and operational data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action for existing wells within the Area of Review
rubrics_metrics.description: UIC permitting authorities may require corrective action for existing wells within the area of review to ensure protection of underground sources of drinking water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrective actions are imposed by the permitting authority as needed to protect USDWs based on the AOR and site-specific information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on movement of fluid into USDWs (40 CFR 144.12(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: See 40 CFR 144.12(b) (prohibition of movement of fluid into USDWs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and operators must demonstrate that injection activities will not result in movement of fluids into USDWs in violation of this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class VI injection well construction requirements (40 CFR 146.86(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: See 40 CFR 146.86(a)(1) (Class VI injection well construction requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit applications must meet the statutory/regulatory construction standards specified in the cited provision (e.g., casing, cementing, well integrity) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class VI injection well operation requirements (40 CFR 146.*)
rubrics_metrics.description: See 40 CFR 146(a) (Class VI injection well operation requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational practices, monitoring, reporting, and other operational obligations for Class VI wells are governed by the relevant subparts of 40 CFR part 146 and must be addressed in permits and MRV plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency and remedial response requirements (40 CFR 146.94)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits and plans should include measures and procedures for emergency response and remedial actions in the event of unintended releases or endangerment of USDWs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seismic history and induced seismicity consideration (40 CFR 146.82(a)(3)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: See 40 CFR 146.82(a)(3)(v) (requiring the permit applicant to submit and the permitting authority to consider information on the seismic history including the presence and depth of seismic sources and a determination that the seismicity would not interfere with containment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide seismic history, identify seismic sources and depths, and include a determination (supported by analysis) that seismicity would not compromise containment of injected CO2; permitting authorities must consider this information during review.
